clue.text: Say "orifice of intercourse" is a traditional way of getting one's member back in action

definitions.text: a traditional way of getting one's member back in action

parts.note: to say something is to state it
an orifice is an opening
taken as written
a parliament was originally a parley, a talk or conference, so intercourse in the old sense of conversation and dealings

explanation.surface: A smutty line about sex as an old-fashioned way to restore a flagging member, in Private Eye's schoolboy style.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'member' is a Member of Parliament: the monarch's formal opening of a new session is what sends MPs back to work.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial start of each parliamentary session is a long-standing ritual that returns MPs to their business at Westminster.

clue.text: Offering to re-shape butt, that is, right?

indicators.note: re-shaping something gives it a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are right to offer a reshaped bottom as a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute is something given as a mark of respect, a gift or offering.

clue.text: Society girl would gobble one for a piece of jewellery

indicators.note: gobbling takes something inside, so one letter goes into the girl's name

parts.note: Tara Palmer-Tomkinson was the best-known society 'It girl' of the late 1990s
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A greedy debutante would swallow anything in exchange for a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head, an item of jewellery.

clue.text: N.B. society is undone by filth

indicators.note: undoing something takes it apart, so these letters are put back together differently

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning note that polite society is being ruined by filth.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscenity means indecent or offensive material, which is filth in the moral sense.

clue.text: Love god, going round bend, that not even the Danes want!

definitions.text: that not even the Danes want

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love
a U-bend, the U-shaped section of a pipe

explanation.surface: Cupid, gone a bit mad, is something nobody wants, not even the Danes.
explanation.walkthrough: Denmark voted against joining the euro in its September 2000 referendum, while Britain was still debating it.
explanation.definitionFit: The single European currency was rejected by Danish voters, so it is money even Denmark refused.

clue.text: Botham ("'Hello, son") gets chop. (See me, Ed.)

parts.note: Ian Botham, the England cricketer
hi is a greeting
to lop is to chop off

explanation.surface: A garbled sports headline about the cricketer Botham being axed, with an editor's note scrawled on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Hislop is the editor of Private Eye, where this puzzle ran, so 'See me, Ed.' is the editor speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The magazine's editor is the 'Ed.' signing the note, so the definition is a self-reference by Private Eye's own editor.

clue.text: Perhaps I spy a tart — a dish!

parts.note: I spy is an example of a game, so 'perhaps' marks it as one of many
a tart is a kind of pie

explanation.surface: A man glimpses an attractive woman and calls her a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' and 'dish' both read as slang for an attractive woman; here they are pastry and food.
explanation.definitionFit: A game pie is a baked pastry filled with venison, pheasant or similar meat, served as a meal.

clue.text: One meets the nastiest sort of hospital employee

indicators.note: one piece meets the other, joined side by side

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: sorting puts things in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: You meet the nastiest kind of person who works in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: An anaesthetist is the hospital doctor who puts patients to sleep before surgery.

clue.text: What Andrew offers us makes Hitler companion appear full of sex appeal!

indicators.note: one piece is full of another, holding it inside

parts.note: Eva Braun was Hitler's companion
'it' is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Andrew's offering makes Hitler's mistress look sexy.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew is Andrew Lloyd Webber, who wrote the musical about Eva Perón, not Prince Andrew or Hitler's Eva.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is the stage musical by Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice, a show he presents to audiences.

clue.text: One whose struggle to be free amuses us

definitions.text: One whose struggle to be free amuses us

parts.words: One whose struggle to be free amuses us
parts.note: a performer who entertains by wriggling out of chains, locks and straitjackets

explanation.definitionFit: An escapologist is a stage entertainer, like Houdini, whose act is escaping from restraints.

clue.text: Tough bloke who finds pick-ups a cinch?

definitions.text: Tough bloke who finds pick-ups a cinch?

parts.words: Tough bloke who finds pick-ups a cinch
parts.note: pick-ups sound like chatting up women, but here they are lifts of heavy weights

explanation.definitionFit: A strongman is a muscular performer or competitor who lifts enormous weights with ease.

clue.text: Like suffering a reverse in vulgar campaign

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

parts.note: crude means vulgar

indicators.note: a word that suffers a reverse is turned the other way round

parts.note: as means like

explanation.surface: Someone apparently suffers a setback in a crude campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade is a vigorous campaign for a cause, from the medieval holy wars.

clue.text: On Saturday, act like William Hague — do something dotty!

parts.note: S as a short form of Saturday
the Tory leader William Hague boasted in 2000 of drinking fourteen pints a day as a youth, so to act like him is to tipple, drink habitually

explanation.surface: A satirical suggestion that copying the Tory leader on a Saturday is a mad thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipple is to paint or engrave using small dots, so it is literally doing something with dots.

clue.text: Before Nazi paramilitary crowd

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force

explanation.surface: A crowd gathering ahead of a Nazi militia.
explanation.definitionFit: To press is to crowd or push together, and a press is also a dense crowd.

clue.text: Putting two and two together, having an erection is what you'd expect of a judge

definitions.text: what you'd expect of a judge

parts.note: adding numbers is summing
up describes something standing erect

explanation.surface: A ribald take on a judge drawing conclusions.
explanation.definitionFit: At the end of a trial the judge reviews the evidence for the jury in a summary, the summing-up.

clue.text: Unruly violent Poles strapped

indicators.note: something unruly is out of order, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: N and S, the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Rowdy Polish men are tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strapped' reads as tied up; it is the slang sense, short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped for cash means having no money, and insolvent means unable to pay debts.

clue.text: Greene's crazy, having it off in a national park!

indicators.note: crazy means wild or mixed up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky story of the novelist Graham Greene going wild with a sexual romp in a nature reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti in Tanzania is a famous protected wildlife reserve, a national park.

clue.text: Heavens! Mother's taken flipping Hattersley for Ken Livingstone!

indicators.note: Mother's has taken the next piece on, so it follows straight after her

parts.note: Lord! is an exclamation like Heavens!
ma means mother

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: Roy Hattersley, the Labour politician

explanation.surface: An exclamation that Mother has taken the Labour veteran Roy Hattersley in place of Ken Livingstone.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone became London's first elected Mayor in 2000; the ceremonial Lord Mayor is a separate City of London post, so the definition is a loose jibe.
explanation.definitionFit: Livingstone held the top civic office in London, its mayoralty, the role the setter grandly titles here.

clue.text: Come across and arrest model with nothing on

parts.note: to run someone in is to arrest them
the Model T Ford
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Finding and arresting a nude model.
explanation.definitionFit: To run into someone is to meet them by chance, the same as coming across them.

clue.text: My word! One's dropped a low type

indicators.note: one letter is dropped, and the clue names it as a

parts.note: parole is a word of honour, a promise given as one's word

explanation.surface: An exclamation at someone dropping to a lowly type.
explanation.definitionFit: Prole, short for proletarian, is a dismissive term for a working-class person, someone of low status.

clue.text: Address love quota …

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
a ration is a fixed allowance or quota

explanation.surface: A speech about a quota of love, running on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal speech, which is what an address is.

clue.text: The dope to do some bathroom DIY? That's Arafat to Barak

parts.note: gen and dope both mean information
tiling is typical bathroom DIY

explanation.surface: Peace-talk gossip about the Palestinian and Israeli leaders Arafat and Barak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests a fool or a drug; here it is information.
explanation.definitionFit: To the Jewish Israeli prime minister Barak, the Palestinian leader Arafat is a non-Jew, a gentile.

clue.text: … in case a gerbil is hot

indicators.note: the answer is found in these words, spanning them

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of case, all of a, and the start of gerbil

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, an allusion to the notorious rumour about Richard Gere and a gerbil.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot for something means keen and impatient for it, like eager.

clue.text: One who would have a bearing on the destruction of a Zion?

definitions.text: One who would have a bearing on the destruction of a Zion?

parts.note: NE, north-east, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: destroying something breaks it into pieces, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone who would contribute to destroying Zion, the Jewish homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a compass bearing placed on a wrecked 'a Zion'.
explanation.definitionFit: A neo-Nazi is a modern follower of Nazism, and antisemitic, so one who would help destroy Zion.

clue.text: Stimulant one, er, gets after work

indicators.note: these pieces come after the first one

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
I is the Roman numeral one
um and er are both hesitations

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly admits to taking a stimulant after work.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is a narcotic drug, here loosely called a stimulant as a substance taken for its effect.

clue.text: Impiety eagerly awaiting, we hear, a religious institution

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the pieces are matched by sound, not spelling

parts.note: an impiety is a sin and eagerly awaiting is agog, so sin agog, which spoken aloud matches the place of worship

explanation.surface: Wickedness eagerly expected at a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A synagogue is a Jewish house of worship and the congregation it serves.

clue.text: Thicko ex-dictator gets round Tories' leader

parts.note: Idi Amin, the former Ugandan dictator
O is round

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: T is the first letter of Tories

explanation.surface: A former tyrant gets round a Conservative leader, who is called a thicko.
explanation.definitionFit: Thicko is British slang for a stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: See 1
